newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TRANSVAAL ON TOP AS QUEENSLAND STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TRANSVAAL ON TOP AS QUEENSLAND STRUGGLE.

text.p: A revitalised Transvaal have romped into an early lead after three rounds of the Super 12 tournament involving the top southern hemisphere provincial sides.

The South Africans registered their third successive win with a 47-29 victory over Otago last Friday, in sharp contrast to last year when they lost their first four matches in Australia and New Zealand.

But it is the demise of Queensland which is currently raising as many eyebrows. The Reds won the Super 10 competition in 1994 and 1995 and were semifinalists in the expanded tournament last year, yet have now lost all three games in 1997.

After losing at home to Australian Capital Territory (ACT) in the opening round, Queensland have lost both their matches in South Africa, 14-3 to Northern Transvaal and 35-24 on Saturday to Free State.
The Wallaby-studded side scored three tries against the Free State Cheetahs, but were reliant on the individual brilliance of lock John Eales for two of them.
With Tim Horan playing his second game out of position at fullback, they never sparked and coach John Connolly has much to do before his side's next match against Waikato in Hamilton next week.

Transvaal meanwhile have responded well to new captain Kobus Wiese and, after an unconvincing display against Free State, have been good value for their victories over ACT (44-36) and Otago at Ellis Park.

The South African sides have all had soft starts at home this year, but familiar problems away from home were exposed in Wellington on Sunday where the Hurricanes walloped Northern Transvaal 64-32, scoring eight tries to four in the process.
Natal, losing finalists to Auckland last year, have nevertheless begun impressively again with straight home wins in Durban over Otago (75-43) and ACT (35-26).

Despite losing key personnel such as wing James Small and lock Steve Atherton over the close season, the Sharks have been able to maintain their expansive style of rugby based on a rock-solid defence.

Elsewhere, New South Wales included David Campese in their 25-8 win over Canterbury in Sydney and defending champions Auckland opened proceedings at their new Albany stadium with a 26-16 win against Waikato.

Auckland are also unbeaten after three games, the highlight being a thrilling 40-40 draw with Northern Transvaal two weeks ago. Waikato had previously beaten New South Wales and Wellington before succumbing to the Blues.
